'''Raquel Prado''' (born 1970) is a Venezuelan [[Bayesian inference|Bayesian]] statistician. She is a professor of statistics in the [[Jack Baskin School of Engineering]] of the [[University of California, Santa Cruz]],{{r|profile}} and has been elected president of the [[International Society for Bayesian Analysis]] for the 2019 term.{{r|alumelect}}

==Contributions==
Prado specializes in [[Bayesian inference]] for [[time series]] data.{{r|profile}} With Mike West, she is the author of the book ''Time Series: Modeling, Computation, and Inference'' (Texts in Statistical Science, CRC Press, 2010).{{r|ts}}
 
==Education and career==
Prado was born on 24 April 1970, in [[Caracas]],
and graduated from [[Simón Bolívar University (Venezuela)|Simón Bolívar University]] in 1993.{{r|duke}}
She completed her Ph.D. in statistics at [[Duke University]] in 1998. Her dissertation, ''Latent Structure in Non-Stationary Time Series'', was supervised by Mike West.{{r|duke|mgp}}

After completing her Ph.D. she returned to Simón Bolívar University as a faculty member before moving to Santa Cruz.{{r|biv}}

==Recognition==
In 1999, Prado and her co-authors Andrew Krystal and Mike West won the Outstanding Statistical Application Award of the [[American Statistical Association]] for their work on statistical analysis of [[electroencephalography]] data.{{r|outapp}}
In 2013, Prado became a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]].{{r|fellow}}
